Test: fossil age-range outliers

Source: R/test-docs.R
test_age_range_outlier.Rd

Flags fossil records whose age range (max_age - min_age) lies above the upper fence of the ranges of the other records of their taxon (Q75 + mltpl x IQR, or median + mltpl x MAD). A record dated only to a long period among records dated to stages is the typical case. With level = "all" the fence is taken over the whole input instead of per taxon, as in CoordinateCleaner's dataset-level cf_range(taxon = ""). A fixed limit in million years needs no test: the range stays a raw column and is cut in tally_flags().

Fields

min_age, max_age, species.

Settings

settings = list(age_range_outlier = list(...)) with method ("quantile"), mltpl (5), size_thresh (7), uniq_loc (FALSE) and level ("taxon").

CoordinateCleaner

Equivalent to cf_range() with method = "quantile" or "mad"; identical flags. With uniq_loc = TRUE, CoordinateCleaner also flags records of other taxa that happen to share a flagged range width; here the flag goes to the records with the same taxon, coordinates and ages.

See also

flag_occurrences(), flag_tests(), test_age_equal

Other tests: test_age_equal, test_age_outlier, test_aohi, test_basis, test_capital, test_centroid, test_country_mismatch, test_dataset_ddmm, test_dataset_rounded, test_duplicate, test_equal, test_establishment, test_gbif_headquarters, test_gbif_issue, test_habitat, test_institution, test_invalid, test_outlier, test_range, test_sea, test_spatiotemporal_outlier, test_urban, test_zero

Examples

x <- data.frame(accepted_name = "A", min_ma = 20, max_ma = c(rep(21, 20), 60))
flag_occurrences(x, tests = "age_range_outlier",
                 columns = occ_columns(species = "accepted_name"))$flag_age_range_outlier
